steps.title: Prepare homogenization buffer
steps.instruction: Make a homogenization buffer containing 50 mM TEAB and 8 M urea (see Recipes).

steps.title: Homogenize mouse tissue
steps.instruction: Grind 50 mg frozen mouse organ tissue on dry ice with ~1 mL homogenization buffer (≈50 mg/mL) using a Dounce grinder, then homogenize in an Omni bead tube at 5 m/s for 30 s, centrifuge 14 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, and transfer the supernatant to a new tube kept on ice.

substeps.instruction: Place the microcentrifuge tube with tissue and the Dounce grinder on dry ice.
Weigh 50 mg tissue into the Dounce grinder.
Add ~1 mL homogenization buffer, grind until homogenized while keeping the sample on dry ice.
Transfer the lysate to an Omni bead homogenizer tube.
Run the Omni homogenizer at 5 m/s for 30 s.
Centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant into a fresh microcentrifuge tube and keep on ice.

steps.title: Quantify protein by BCA assay
steps.instruction: Perform a BCA assay using a 125–2000 µg/mL standard curve and sample dilutions (10‑, 20‑, 40‑fold); add 25 µL standard or sample plus 200 µL working reagent (50:1 A:B) in a 96‑well plate, incubate 30 min at 37 °C, read absorbance at 562 nm, calculate concentrations, and adjust samples to 2 500 µg/mL (100 µL) on ice.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a standard curve ranging from 125 to 2000 µg/mL.
Dilute samples 10‑, 20‑, and 40‑fold as needed.
In each well add 25 µL standard or diluted sample.
Add 200 µL BCA working reagent (reagent A:B = 50:1).
Cover plate with aluminum foil and incubate 30 min at 37 °C.
Measure absorbance at 562 nm.
Use GraphPad Prism (linear regression) to determine protein concentrations.
Dilute or concentrate samples to 2 500 µg/mL (final volume 100 µL) and keep on ice.
Optional: freeze samples at –20 °C for next‑day use or at –80 °C for long‑term storage; thaw at 4 °C before further steps.

steps.title: Add BSA and DTT, then denature
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.2 mg/mL BSA in water and spike each sample with 10 µL; prepare 100 mM DTT in water, add 25 µL to each tube, vortex, then denature proteins at 34 °C in a shaking water bath (100 rpm) for 30 min (temperature must not exceed 35 °C).

substeps.instruction: Set shaking water bath to 34 °C and set centrifuge temperature to 10 °C (if applicable).
Make BSA solution 0.2 mg/mL in Milli‑Q water; add 10 µL to each sample (optional).
Make DTT solution 100 mM in Milli‑Q water; add 25 µL to each tube and vortex.
Wear appropriate PPE when handling DTT.
Place tubes in shaking water bath at 34 °C, 100 rpm, for 30 min.
Monitor temperature to stay ≤35 °C (urea decomposes above this).

steps.title: Alkylate with IAA and precipitate proteins
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL 200 mM IAA (prepared in water) to each sample, incubate 30 min at ~20 °C in the dark, then precipitate by sequentially adding ice‑cold water (160 µL), methanol (320 µL), and chloroform (160 µL) (1:2:1), vortex, centrifuge 10 000 × g for 5 min at 10 °C, remove chloroform (bottom) and methanol/water (top) layers, wash pellet with 200 µL ice‑cold methanol, remove wash, and resuspend pellet in 130 µL 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate (pH ≈ 8) containing 3 % w/v DOC.

substeps.instruction: Place water, methanol, and chloroform on ice.
Prepare IAA 200 mM in water; add 25 µL to each sample.
Protect from light; incubate at room temperature (~20 °C) in the dark for 30 min.
Add ice‑cold water 160 µL, then methanol 320 µL, then chloroform 160 µL (1:2:1).
Vortex after all solvents are added.
Centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 5 min at 10 °C.
Using a gel tip, carefully remove the bottom chloroform layer.
Then remove the top methanol/water layer.
Add 200 µL ice‑cold methanol to wash the pellet; remove the wash with a gel tip.
Resuspend the pellet in 130 µL 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate (pH ≈ 8) with 3 % DOC, scrape tube walls and pipette up/down.
Store at –80 °C if not proceeding immediately; thaw at 4 °C before next step.

steps.title: PCT‑assisted trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Reconstitute lyophilized TPCK‑treated trypsin to 1 mg/mL with 500 µL Milli‑Q water, add 10 µL (10 µg) trypsin to each 250 µg protein sample (1:25 w/w), vortex 3–5 s, transfer 138 µL to labeled microtubes, cap, place in Barocycler cartridge, press PRECHARGE three times, run 75 pressure cycles (60 s each: 50 s high pressure, 10 s ambient) at ~25.5 psi and 35–37 °C, then repeat a second digestion by adding another 10 µL trypsin and running the same Barocycler program.

substeps.instruction: Turn on Barocycler and air compressor; set water bath to 35–37 °C.
Add 500 µL Milli‑Q water to lyophilized trypsin (1 mg/mL); vortex.
Add 10 µL trypsin (10 µg) to each sample containing 250 µg protein (1:25 ratio); vortex 3–5 s.
Transfer 138 µL of each sample to individually labeled microtubes using gel tips.
Cap tubes with microcap tool.
Load tubes into Barocycler cartridge and insert cartridge into the instrument.
Press PRECHARGE three times to prime lines.
Run digestion: 75 cycles, 60 s per cycle (50 s high pressure, 10 s ambient), pressure ≈25.5 psi, temperature 35–37 °C.
After run, remove cartridge with magnetic rod, remove caps.
Add another 10 µL trypsin (maintaining 1:25 w/w) to each tube, reseal, and repeat the Barocycler program (steps above).
After the second run, remove cartridge, caps, and place tubes in a microtube rack.

steps.title: Desalt and precipitate DOC
steps.instruction: Add 15 µL 5 % formic acid in 50:50 acetonitrile:water to 0.5 mL tubes, then add 135 µL of each digested sample, vortex (white precipitate forms), centrifuge 10 000 × g for 5 min at 10 °C, transfer supernatant to a new tube, centrifuge again 10 000 × g for 5 min at 10 °C, then transfer 100 µL supernatant to an amber glass vial with a bottom spring insert; samples are ready for LC‑MS/MS or can be stored at –80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 5 % formic acid in a 50:50 mixture of acetonitrile and water.
Aliquot 15 µL of this solution into each 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 135 µL of the respective trypsin‑digested sample using a gel tip; vortex to mix (DOC precipitates as a white solid).
Centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 5 min at 10 °C.
Transfer the clear supernatant to a new 0.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge the transferred supernatant again at 10 000 × g for 5 min at 10 °C.
Move 100 µL of the final supernatant into an amber glass vial containing a bottom spring glass insert.
Proceed to LC‑MS/MS analysis or store at –80 °C (thaw at 4 °C before use).
